headline: 11-year-old Linux kernel bug lets attackers crash servers remotely
summary: An 11-year-old Linux kernel vulnerability called NoisyTCP can be used to remotely crash servers running common services with default configurations.

claims.statement: NoisyTCP is an 11-year-old Linux kernel vulnerability that lets attackers remotely crash Linux servers.

sources.quote: New NoisyTCP vulnerability lets attackers crash Linux servers
NoisyTCP bug gives Linux servers a remote crash problem 11 years in the making

claims.statement: The flaw affects systems running Nginx, Apache, and SSH servers with default configurations.

sources.quote: lets attackers crash systems running Nginx, Apache, and SSH servers with default configurations

claims.statement: The flaw can take down an entire host even when the vulnerable service runs inside a container.

sources.quote: Flaw can take down an entire host, even when the vulnerable service is running inside a container
